name: Hex Comparadun (Extended Body)
imitates: A big extended-body Hexagenia dun for the twilight and night hatch; the deer hair wing and optional hackle make it float well when you cannot see it.
recipe: 30 lb monofilament or wild boar hair
Optional dry fly hackle behind the wing

steps.text: Wrap thread on the shank and use it to bind a long piece of 30 lb monofilament to the hook. Leave it long so you have something to grab.
Tie in ginger Microfibett tail fibers at the bend so the tail extends well past the hook; the mono can be the same length and is trimmed later.
Reverse the hook 180 degrees and stick the point into the vise jaws, which makes tying the extended body on the mono much easier.
Wrap thread around the mono and tail fibers as far back as the body extension needs to be.
Twist tan-yellow dubbing on the thread and wrap it along the mono toward the hook bend, then turn the hook back around in the vise.
Trim the excess mono, move the thread forward and tie in a deer hair clump about as long as the whole body as a comparadun wing.

Pull the wing back and tie a smaller clump in front of it, tips toward the bend, to hold the wing up. Wrap back and dub the rest of the body, add 3-4 turns of hackle behind the wing if you like, then dub in front of the wing and whip finish.
Trim the hackle underneath so the fly lies flush on the water. The finished flies.
